'''Michael John Wingfield''' (born 21 April 1954) is a South African academic and scientist who studies [[plant pathology]] and [[biological control]]. He was the founding director of the [[Forestry and Agricultural Biotechnology Institute]], [[University of Pretoria]]. Wingfield has authored or co-authored over 1,000 scientific publications and is considered a leading expert in the field of forest health and invasive species. He has received numerous awards and honours throughout his career, including  [[Harry Oppenheimer Fellowship Award]] and John Herschel Medal, the highest accolade from the [[Royal Society of South Africa]]. He is also a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of South Africa]] and the [[African Academy of Sciences]]. Wingfield has had several [[Fungus|fungi]] named after him.

== Life and career ==

Wingfield |url=https://www.apsnet.org/members/give-awards/awards/Fellows/Pages/MichaelJWingfield.aspx |access-date=26 December 2022 |website=Michael J. === Career ===

While working at the Plant Protection Research Institute of Stellenbosch University, Wingfield started the country's first forest pathology research programme in 1978. After earning his PhD, he continued the program's expansion. In 1990, Wingfield was promoted to professor in the Department of Microbiology and Biochemistry at the [[University of the Free State]] after relocating there in 1988. Wingfield was named the Mondi Paper Co. Ltd. Chair in [[forest pathology]] in 1994.<ref name=":5" />
 
Wingfield was the founding director of the [[Forestry and Agricultural Biotechnology Institute]] (FABI), [[University of Pretoria]], in until 2017.<ref name=":0" /> FABI was founded in 1998 due to Wingfield's work in 1990 to create the Tree Protection Co-operative Programme.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Michael Wingfield {{!}} World Forestry Congress {{!}} Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations |url=https://www.fao.org/about/meetings/world-forestry-congress-xiv/speakers/michael-wingfield/en/ |access-date=26 December 2022 |website=www.fao.org |archive-date=26 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226160237/https://www.fao.org/about/meetings/world-forestry-congress-xiv/speakers/michael-wingfield/en/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He continued as a professor at FABI and an advisor to the Executive Board of the University of Pretoria.<ref name=":0" />
 
Wingfield was the director of the Centre of Excellence in Tree Health Biotechnology, National Research Foundation, and the President of the [[International Union of Forest Research Organizations]] (IUFRO) between 2014 and 2019.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> His collaboration with Chinese academics led to the formation of the CERC/FABI Tree Protection Programme (CFTPP),<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=13 October 2017 |title=Prof Mike Wingfield receives Chinese Government Friendship Award {{!}} the University of Pretoria |url=https://www.up.ac.za/fabi/news/post_2578540-prof-mike-wingfield-receives-chinese-government-friendship-award |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226153403/https://www.up.ac.za/fabi/news/post_2578540-prof-mike-wingfield-receives-chinese-government-friendship-award |archive-date=26 December 2022 |access-date=26 December 2022 |website=www.up.ac.za |language=en}}</ref> a joint venture between the [[Forestry and Agricultural Biotechnology Institute|FABI]] and the [[China Eucalyptus Research Centre]] (CERC), in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Memorandum of Understanding established between FABI and CERC |url=https://www.fabinet.up.ac.za/index.php/news-item?id=307 |access-date=10 August 2023 |website=FABI |language=en-gb}}</ref> CFTPP was renamed to RIFT-FABI Tree Protection Programme (RFTPP).<ref>{{Cite web |title=RIFT-FABI Tree Protection Programme |url=https://www.fabinet.up.ac.za/index.php/research-groups/cerc-fabi-tree-protection-programme |access-date=10 August 2023 |website=FABI}}</ref>
